title: Fourier Series and Transforms — practice exam

questions.question: What does the coefficient a0 represent in a Fourier series?
options: The amplitude of the first harmonic
The phase offset of the fundamental
The average value of the function over one period
questions.explanation: a0 is the DC term: the mean of the function across one full period. The harmonics an and bn describe variation about that mean.

questions.question: For an even function on a symmetric interval, which coefficients vanish?
questions.explanation: For even f, the product f(x)·sin(nx) is odd, so it integrates to zero across a symmetric interval and every bn vanishes.

questions.question: State, in one sentence, what a Fourier series lets you do to a periodic function.
questions.expected: says it rewrites a periodic function as a sum of sines and cosines (1); notes each component carries its own frequency and weight (1)

questions.question: Name one physical situation where decomposing a signal into frequencies is useful, and say why.
questions.expected: names a valid situation — audio equalisation, filtering noise from a measurement, spectral analysis, image compression (1); gives the reason: once separated, the frequency components can be treated independently (1)

questions.question: How many Dirichlet conditions must a function satisfy for its Fourier series to converge?
questions.explanation: Three: the function must be absolutely integrable over a period, have a finite number of extrema in that period, and a finite number of finite discontinuities.

questions.question: At a point where a function has a jump discontinuity, its Fourier series converges to:
options: The value on the left of the jump
The value on the right of the jump
It does not converge at all
questions.explanation: The series converges to the average of the left and right limits — the midpoint — regardless of how the function itself is defined at that point.

questions.question: Write the integral expression for bn and explain what the sine factor is doing.
questions.expected: gives bn = 1/pi times the integral of f(x)·sin(nx) dx (1); states it is taken over one full period (1); explains the sine factor projects f onto that harmonic, measuring how much of that frequency is present (1)

questions.question: Explain why the Dirichlet conditions are a constraint rather than a formality.
questions.expected: states that the conditions bound what the series can represent (1); gives a function that violates them, such as one with infinitely many discontinuities or one that is not absolutely integrable (1); draws the consequence: the series need not converge to the function, so results derived from the expansion stop being valid (1)

questions.question: The Fast Fourier Transform reduces the cost of computing a discrete transform from O(n^2) to:
questions.explanation: The FFT exploits symmetry in the roots of unity to split the transform recursively, giving O(n log n) — the result that makes spectral methods practical at scale.

questions.question: Describe the Gibbs phenomenon and explain why adding more terms does not remove it.
questions.expected: describes the partial sums overshooting near a jump discontinuity (1); gives the size of the overshoot as roughly 9% of the jump height (1); states that adding terms narrows the region but does not shrink the overshoot (1); explains the cause: convergence there is pointwise rather than uniform (1)
